# Session-corpus config (v1)

Schema for `.tera/session-corpus/<name>.hcl` config files. Each decodes to `pkg/config.SessionCorpusBlock` — the store-wide mechanics of the ADR-114 session corpus, which no `activity_partition` recipe could own (*what* a partition keeps and for how long is that recipe's `retention` block). A singleton kind: at most one `session_corpus` block across the vault. Relocated out of the bootstrap-HCL kernel by ADR-122 D5, and the kernel spelling is retired rather than retained as an escape hatch — an edit here reaches the running writer's census ticker on the next reload, so a second place to author it would be a place a reload does not look.

| | |
|---|---|
| Registry name | `config/session-corpus` |
| Regime | persisted |
| Identity regime | `singleton` — the kind itself is the identity; neither the stem nor a label carries meaning (ADR-087 D3) |
| Current version | `v1` |
| Supported versions | `v1` |
| HCL block | `session_corpus` |
| Loader directory | `.tera/session-corpus/<name>.hcl` |
| Go source | `github.com/kottera/kottera/pkg/config.SessionCorpusBlock` |
| Served at | `GET /api/v1/schemas/config/session-corpus/reference` |

## Example

A minimal `session-corpus`: every required attribute, exactly one member of each closed union, and nothing optional beyond what the kind would otherwise render empty. It is generated from the same source these tables are, and the same bytes are run through `tera validate` by the ADR-087 D9 pattern-transfer test — so it cannot describe a shape the loader does not accept.

Cross-references name the other kinds' examples (`example-worker`, `example-tool`, …) because every kind's example is validated together with the rest, as one vault.

`.tera/session-corpus/example-session-corpus.hcl`:

```hcl
version = "v1"

session_corpus {}
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Required | Default | Since | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `census_flush_interval` | string | no | — | — | — | How often the session corpus appends its per-partition census tally to disk. Unset takes the store's own default. Must be positive: a non-positive interval is a ticker that never fires, which would leave the tally in memory until shutdown. An edit takes effect on the next reload — the running writer's ticker is reset, and the tally already pending is appended once, on the next flush under the new cadence. |
